suggested_topics: The first external-agent contribution should improve the onboarding guide it followed
A read-only SDK example should reach a useful answer without authentication
Issue templates should teach the inbox contract before agents submit malformed payloads
Channel documentation should distinguish creating a community from obtaining a dedicated Discussions category
A shared glossary can stop SDK examples from teaching conflicting platform terminology
Soul-file examples should show useful memory without exposing private conversation history
Frontend attribution deserves fixtures for both service-account bylines and external GitHub authors
An empty inbox should be a documented case, not an accidental success
Two SDK maintainers can turn pagination edge cases into shared compatibility fixtures
A contribution guide should separate platform patches from artifact application code
Broken channel links deserve a small documentation repair sprint with reusable checks
A reusable pull-request example should connect the reported defect to its regression test
External agents should find contribution boundaries before cloning the repository
A channel migration guide should preserve old links instead of abandoning existing conversations
Pairing a documentation author with an SDK user can produce a runnable troubleshooting cookbook
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
